issues: Demonstrates open()'s two-argument signature and the 'w' (create+write) and 'a' (append) modes, plus manual .close(); does not demonstrate 'r' (read) mode or the default-to-'r'-when-omitted part of f1, which appear later in the video (Reading a File chapter, outside this range) -- f1 only partially covered.
Also demonstrates an 'x' (create-only) mode not named in f1's required statement; this is extra accurate info, not a contradiction.

proposals.transcript_evidence: so I'm gonna remove this one and start with select and now I cannot use star because I don't want to have all the columns
issues: This video never uses the AS keyword/column aliasing (f2 not covered) -- only the SELECT-list and FROM mechanics (f1, f3) are taught.

Start is placed a few seconds after the task is introduced, to skip past a comparison to the video's earlier 'select *' task ('the difference from the previous one') that would otherwise read as an unresolved backward reference.

proposals.label: Power BI's model view: telling a one-to-many relationship from a one-to-one by which side repeats the key
proposals.transcript_evidence: So, for the first customer, Maria did place two orders. So, on the left side it is one, on the right side it is many.
issues: The video never says 'foreign key' -- it shows the same mechanism (the connecting customer-ID column repeating on the 'many' side) through Power BI's model-view UI rather than naming the FK column, so f2's foreign-key terminology is inferred rather than stated verbatim.

Range starts with a short one-to-one example (402-432) before the one-to-many example (432-468) because the one-to-many example reuses the 'check the keys for duplicates' method taught during the one-to-one example ('same thing, we're going to check the values inside the keys') -- cutting straight to 432 would leave that method unresolved.

proposals.label: Tracing one query's real execution order: FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY
proposals.transcript_evidence: the first thing that's going to happen is that SQL going to execute the from
issues: Start is placed ~2s after the 'SQL execution order' chapter marker (114) to skip the phrase 'as we learned', a backward reference to the earlier 'five types of SQL filters' section that this range doesn't otherwise need.
f2 (alias usable in ORDER BY/GROUP BY but not WHERE/HAVING) is not covered -- this video only walks the clause order itself, not alias scoping.

This video's walkthrough also names the TOP clause as a final step; TOP/LIMIT is allowed knowledge for this concept (not blocked), so it doesn't block the range, but it isn't one of this concept's required facts either.
